stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $A = \mathbb{F}_p[T]$ be the polynomial ring in one variable over
$\mathbb{F}_p$. Let $A_{perf}$  denote the perfect closure of $A$.
Then $A \rightarrow A_{perf}$ is flat and formally unramified,
but not formally \'etale.
hypotheses:
Let $A = \mathbb{F}_p[T]$ be the polynomial ring in one variable over
$\mathbb{F}_p$. Let $A_{perf}$  denote the perfect closure of $A$.
conclusions:
$A \rightarrow A_{perf}$ is flat and formally unramified,
but not formally \'etale.

reason: Frobenius on F_p[T] is free and faithfully flat, so the perfection is flat. Perfection kills relative differentials, proving formal unramifiedness; the cotangent triangle gives a nonzero degree −1 cotangent class, ruling out formal smoothness and hence formal étaleness.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a regular local ring of characteristic
$p > 0$. Suppose $[\kappa : \kappa^p] < \infty$. Then $A$ is excellent
if and only if $A \to A^\wedge$ is formally \'etale.
hypotheses:
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a regular local ring of characteristic
$p > 0$. Suppose $[\kappa : \kappa^p] < \infty$.
conclusions:
$A$ is excellent
if and only if $A \to A^\wedge$ is formally \'etale.

reason: The prior completion criterion gives one direction and formal unramifiedness. Under excellence and regularity, Néron–Popescu desingularization writes the completion as a filtered colimit of smooth algebras, yielding formal smoothness and hence formal étaleness.
